import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hilbert's Fifth Problem and the Hilbert–Smith Conjecture

The **Hilbert–Smith conjecture** states that a locally compact topological group acting
continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold must be a
Lie group. It remains open in general; Pardon proved it for 3-manifolds in 2013.
An equivalent formulation: no p-adic integer group `ℤ_[p]` can act faithfully on any
connected finite-dimensional topological manifold.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
- [Pardon 2013, arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)
- [van den Dries–Goldbring, *Hilbert's Fifth Problem*]
  (https://ems.press/journals/lem/articles/13621)
- [arXiv:math/0103145](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103145)
-/

namespace Hilbert5

open scoped Manifold ContDiff EuclideanGeometry

universe u

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
variable {n : ℕ} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
  [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]

/-- A continuous group isomorphism from `G` to an `n`-dimensional real-analytic Lie group. -/
structure LieGroupPresentation (G : Type u) [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] (n : ℕ) where
  carrier : Type u
  [topologicalSpace : TopologicalSpace carrier]
  [group : Group carrier]
  [t2Space : T2Space carrier]
  [secondCountableTopology : SecondCountableTopology carrier]
  [chartedSpace : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) carrier]
  [isManifold : IsManifold (𝓡 n) ω carrier]
  [lieGroup : LieGroup (𝓡 n) ω carrier]
  equiv : G ≃ₜ* carrier

/-- A topological group admits a Lie group structure if it has a `LieGroupPresentation` in some
finite dimension. -/
def AdmitsLieGroupStructure (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n, Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n)

/-- Every finite-dimensional real-analytic Lie group admits a Lie group structure. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem admitsLieGroupStructure_of_lieGroup
    [T2Space G] [SecondCountableTopology G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G]
    [LieGroup (𝓡 n) ω G] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G :=
  ⟨n, ⟨{ carrier := G, equiv := ContinuousMulEquiv.refl G }⟩⟩

/-- A group admitting a Lie group structure is locally compact. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem locallyCompact_of_admitsLieGroupStructure
    (h : AdmitsLieGroupStructure G) : LocallyCompactSpace G := by
  obtain ⟨k, ⟨p⟩⟩ := h
  let := p.topologicalSpace
  let := p.group
  let := p.chartedSpace
  have := (𝓡 k).locallyCompactSpace
  have : LocallyCompactSpace p.carrier :=
    ChartedSpace.locallyCompactSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) p.carrier
  exact p.equiv.toHomeomorph.locallyCompactSpace_iff.mpr inferInstance

/-- **Hilbert–Smith conjecture**: every locally compact topological group acting continuously
and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- The conjecture holds when `G` acts by isometries on a Riemannian manifold, since `G`
embeds as a closed subgroup of the isometry group, which is a Lie group by Myers–Steenrod. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 53 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X]
    [MetricSpace X] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ X]
    (hiso : ∀ g : G, Isometry (g • · : X → X)) :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- Pardon (2013): the Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for 3-dimensional manifolds.
See [arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- Equivalent p-adic formulation: the p-adic integers `ℤ_[p]` cannot act continuously and
faithfully on any connected finite-dimensional topological manifold. By the Gleason–Yamabe
theorem, this is equivalent to `hilbert_smith_conjecture`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_padic_formulation (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    [AddAction (PadicInt p) X] [ContinuousVAdd (PadicInt p) X]
    [FaithfulVAdd (PadicInt p) X] :
    False := by
  sorry

/-- **Hilbert's fifth problem** (Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin, 1952): every Hausdorff,
second-countable topological group modeled on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space is continuously
isomorphic to a real-analytic Lie group.

The input `ChartedSpace` supplies only a topological atlas. The compatible analytic atlas and
analytic group operations belong to the output `LieGroupPresentation`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57]
theorem hilbert_fifth_problem
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [SecondCountableTopology G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G] :
    Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n) := by
  sorry

end Hilbert5

findings.description: The elaborated theorem has neither the parameter n nor a ChartedSpace hypothesis. The section variable at lines 44–45 is unused and is not retained. Consequently, the theorem concerns arbitrary connected Hausdorff spaces, not finite-dimensional manifolds. A concrete counterexample is the additive group ℤ_[2] acting on C(ℤ_[2], ℝ) by (g • f)(x) = f(x + g). This action is continuous and faithful, and the function space is connected and Hausdorff. The group is compact, infinite and totally disconnected, so it cannot be locally Euclidean. The action and the nonexistence of a LieGroupPresentation were verified in Lean without sorryAx. Both spaces in this counterexample are second countable, so this defect is independent of the countability issue.
findings.source_evidence: Tao, Conjecture 2, explicitly requires a “connected finite-dimensional manifold X”: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/. Pardon §1 likewise requires a connected n-manifold: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324.
findings.suggested_fix: Put {n : ℕ} and [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] directly in the theorem's binders, or explicitly include the section's charted-space hypothesis. Merely declaring it as a section variable does not retain it.

findings.description: The elaborated theorem omits both n and the section's ChartedSpace hypothesis. It asserts that ℤ_[p] cannot act continuously and faithfully on any connected Hausdorff space. For p = 2, its hypotheses hold on X = C(ℤ_[2], ℝ), using (g +ᵥ f)(x) = f(x + g). Faithfulness follows by testing continuous distance functions at 0. The scratch file proves a negation of this unrestricted statement without using any admitted theorem, and applying the declaration to this example produces False.
findings.source_evidence: Tao, Conjecture 3: a p-adic group cannot act continuously and effectively on a “connected finite-dimensional manifold X,” not an arbitrary connected Hausdorff space. https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/. See also Pardon's second conjecture in §1: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly bind {n : ℕ} and [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] in this theorem, or explicitly include that section hypothesis.

findings.description: Independently of the missing manifold hypothesis, the conclusion forces SecondCountableTopology G: LieGroupPresentation requires a second-countable carrier and a homeomorphic group isomorphism from G. No corresponding restriction is imposed on G. Let G be the additive group of ℝ³ with the discrete topology, acting by translations on ordinary ℝ³. This is a locally compact topological group with a continuous faithful action on a genuine connected manifold, but G is uncountable discrete and therefore not second countable. Lean verifies that it has no LieGroupPresentation. In the source's convention, it is a legitimate zero-dimensional Lie group.
findings.source_evidence: Tao explicitly clarifies: “I am not requiring manifolds (or Lie groups) here to be second countable.” https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/#comment-474517. His Conjecture 2 imposes no second-countability condition on G.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove global second countability from LieGroupPresentation to match the cited convention, or explicitly state the second-countable version by adding [SecondCountableTopology G]. Make the convention consistent across the action theorems.

findings.description: Although this theorem correctly retains its three-dimensional ChartedSpace assumption, its unrestricted G is incompatible with the second-countable conclusion encoded by AdmitsLieGroupStructure. The discrete additive group of ℝ³ acts continuously, faithfully and transitively on standard ℝ³ by translations. It satisfies every input hypothesis but cannot be homeomorphic to a second-countable carrier. This counterexample and the failure of the conclusion were checked in Lean without sorryAx.
findings.source_evidence: Pardon's abstract states the result for every locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected three-manifold; §1 defines faithful action as a continuous injection into Homeo(M), not a topological embedding. https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324. The cited Tao exposition explicitly does not require Lie groups to be second countable: https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/#comment-474517.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [SecondCountableTopology G] if retaining the current presentation definition, or relax the presentation's countability requirement to use the source's Lie-group convention.

findings.description: The same countability mismatch also makes this variant false, even with a genuine smooth Riemannian metric. Take G to be additive ℝ³ with the discrete topology and X to be standard Euclidean ℝ³. Every translation is an isometry, and all the action, manifold and local-compactness hypotheses hold. Nevertheless, AdmitsLieGroupStructure G is impossible because it would make this uncountable discrete group second countable. The complete example compiles in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: The Hilbert–Smith framework in the cited Tao article allows locally compact groups without global second countability, and its countability clarification explicitly allows such Lie groups. https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/#comment-474517. Myers–Steenrod concerns the isometry group of a connected Riemannian manifold; a faithful continuous action need not identify G homeomorphically with its image. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myers%E2%80%93Steenrod_theorem.
findings.suggested_fix: Add [SecondCountableTopology G], or remove the global second-countability requirement from LieGroupPresentation consistently with the cited convention.

findings.description: The hypotheses [MetricSpace X] and [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ X] do not specify a Riemannian manifold with its Riemannian distance. There is no smooth inner product on the tangent bundle and no requirement that the supplied distance be induced by it. Even after making the topologies agree, an arbitrary compatible metric is substantially weaker: every continuous compact-group action on a metrizable space admits a compatible invariant metric. Thus this is not the Riemannian-isometry special case to which Myers–Steenrod applies.
findings.source_evidence: Myers–Steenrod requires a connected Riemannian manifold, with its Riemannian distance; its differentiability theorem applies to distance-preserving maps between such manifolds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myers%E2%80%93Steenrod_theorem. The cited Hilbert–Smith page also specifies a Riemannian manifold for the known Lipschitz-action result: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Supply a smooth Riemannian structure on fun x : X => TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x, using Bundle.RiemannianBundle and IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle, and require IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) X so that the distance used by Isometry is the associated Riemannian distance.

findings.description: The MetricSpace X binder is independent of the earlier TopologicalSpace X. Explicit printing shows that ConnectedSpace, ChartedSpace, IsManifold and ContinuousSMul use the earlier topology, while Isometry uses the later metric. There is no compatibility equation. One may therefore supply the discrete 0/1 metric while keeping the manifold's ordinary topology for its atlas and action. Every group action is isometric for that metric, so the isometry hypothesis adds no restriction. This construction and an application of the theorem using it were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: The source's Riemannian manifold has a single topology, induced by its Riemannian distance; Myers–Steenrod does not concern a metric unrelated to the manifold topology. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myers%E2%80%93Steenrod_theorem. Mathlib's MetricSpace carries its own topology, and the printed declaration retains the two topology arguments independently.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebind X for this variant with [MetricSpace X] first, and formulate all topological, charted-space and action hypotheses using that metric's topology. Alternatively, explicitly require equality with the pre-existing topology. This is separate from supplying the missing Riemannian structure.

findings.description: The docstring's assertion that G “embeds as a closed subgroup of the isometry group” does not follow from a continuous faithful action, even after fixing the other hypotheses. For example, discrete ℚ acts faithfully and isometrically on the usual real line by translations; its image is a nonclosed subgroup of the real translation group.
findings.source_evidence: Pardon §1 explicitly defines a faithful action as a continuous injection into Homeo(M), without a closed-embedding requirement: https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324. Van den Dries–Goldbring, §2, 'Generalities on NSS', item (5), supplies the appropriate alternative: a continuous homomorphism injective near the identity pulls back the no-small-subgroups property. https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/44285?nt=1.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the closed-subgroup explanation with: Myers–Steenrod makes Isom(X) a Lie group; a continuous faithful homomorphism into it gives G no small subgroups; the locally compact NSS characterization then gives a Lie structure on G, with the chosen countability convention handled consistently.

reformulations.difference: The declaration uses the consistently second-countable, fixed-dimension atlas formulation, and puts the analytic structure on a homeomorphically isomorphic carrier rather than directly on G. The cited sources also allow non-second-countable locally Euclidean groups.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An atlas modeled on ℝⁿ gives local Euclidean neighborhoods; conversely, a chart near the identity can be translated to give an atlas. Pulling the output atlas back along the ContinuousMulEquiv gives a compatible analytic group structure on G; conversely, choose G itself as carrier. Topological dimension ensures the same n. The second-countable theorem also yields the broader source version: the identity component of a locally Euclidean group is open and second countable. Apply the theorem to that component, then extend its analytic atlas to the other cosets. Conjugations restrict to continuous Lie-group automorphisms, hence are analytic, so the extended group operations are analytic. Tao explicitly uses this open-Lie-subgroup reduction. Thus the consistent countability restriction here is not the output-only mismatch found in the action theorems.

reformulations.difference: There is no explicit T2Space G assumption, although the locally compact groups in the sources are Hausdorff.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map g ↦ (x ↦ g • x) into X → X with the product topology is continuous by ContinuousSMul and injective by FaithfulSMul. Its codomain is Hausdorff because X is Hausdorff, so G is Hausdorff. The scratch file proves this and the generic equivalence (T2Space G → P) ↔ P under these action hypotheses. The observation also applies to both action variants and is independent of the reported defects.

review.notes: All nine declarations were checked. No additional defect was found in the two proved API lemmas or the consistently second-countable Hilbert-fifth formulation. The three countability findings share one interface mismatch: LieGroupPresentation uses a standard second-countable convention, while those action theorems do not restrict G accordingly. The intended open/solved statuses agree with the current references; McAuley's old proof claim was not treated as an accepted resolution in light of the later and current sources. There are no answer(...) or formal_proof records. The consolidated /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. Its independent counterexample constructions, nonpresentation proofs and Hausdorff equivalence use no sorryAx. Zero-dimensional presentations, nonemptiness, and p = 0, 1, 2 were also checked. The reviewed file was not modified.

submission.summary: Explicitly retained the finite-dimensional manifold hypotheses in both conjectures. Removed global second countability from LieGroupPresentation, matching the cited convention and fixing all three action theorems, with the corresponding API adjustment. The Riemannian variant now uses one metric-induced topology, a smooth Riemannian tangent-bundle structure, and compatibility with its Riemannian distance; its closed-subgroup explanation was also corrected. Required compilation passed with only the five expected sorry warnings, and scratch validation confirmed the corrected signatures and representative examples.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!

continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold must be a

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%E2%80%93Smith_conjecture)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
- [Pardon 2013, arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324)

namespace Hilbert5

open scoped Manifold ContDiff EuclideanGeometry Bundle

universe u

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
variable {n : ℕ} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]

/-- A continuous group isomorphism from `G` to an `n`-dimensional real-analytic Lie group.

Following the cited Hilbert–Smith formulations, no global second-countability condition is
imposed. -/
structure LieGroupPresentation (G : Type u) [TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] (n : ℕ) where
  carrier : Type u
  [topologicalSpace : TopologicalSpace carrier]
  [group : Group carrier]
  [t2Space : T2Space carrier]
  [chartedSpace : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) carrier]
  [isManifold : IsManifold (𝓡 n) ω carrier]
  [lieGroup : LieGroup (𝓡 n) ω carrier]
  equiv : G ≃ₜ* carrier

/-- A topological group admits a Lie group structure if it has a `LieGroupPresentation` in some
finite dimension. -/
def AdmitsLieGroupStructure (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n, Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n)

/-- Every finite-dimensional real-analytic Lie group admits a Lie group structure. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem admitsLieGroupStructure_of_lieGroup
    [T2Space G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G]
    [LieGroup (𝓡 n) ω G] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G :=
  ⟨n, ⟨{ carrier := G, equiv := ContinuousMulEquiv.refl G }⟩⟩

/-- A group admitting a Lie group structure is locally compact. -/
@[category API, AMS 22]
theorem locallyCompact_of_admitsLieGroupStructure
    (h : AdmitsLieGroupStructure G) : LocallyCompactSpace G := by
  obtain ⟨k, ⟨p⟩⟩ := h
  let := p.topologicalSpace
  let := p.group
  let := p.chartedSpace
  have := (𝓡 k).locallyCompactSpace
  have : LocallyCompactSpace p.carrier :=
    ChartedSpace.locallyCompactSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) p.carrier
  exact p.equiv.toHomeomorph.locallyCompactSpace_iff.mpr inferInstance

/-- **Hilbert–Smith conjecture**: every locally compact topological group acting continuously
and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture {n : ℕ}
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- The conjecture holds when `G` acts by isometries on a smooth Riemannian manifold.
By Myers–Steenrod, the isometry group is a Lie group. The continuous faithful homomorphism
into it gives `G` no small subgroups, so `G` is a Lie group. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 53 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.riemannian {X : Type*}
    [MetricSpace X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ X]
    [Bundle.RiemannianBundle (fun x : X => TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle (𝓡 n) ∞ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (fun x : X => TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x)]
    [IsRiemannianManifold (𝓡 n) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X]
    (hiso : ∀ g : G, Isometry (g • · : X → X)) :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- Pardon (2013): the Hilbert–Smith conjecture holds for 3-dimensional manifolds.
See [arXiv:1112.2324](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2324). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_conjecture.variants.dimension_three {X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) X]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [LocallyCompactSpace G]
    [MulAction G X] [ContinuousSMul G X] [FaithfulSMul G X] :
    AdmitsLieGroupStructure G := by
  sorry

/-- Equivalent p-adic formulation: the p-adic integers `ℤ_[p]` cannot act continuously and
faithfully on any connected finite-dimensional topological manifold. By the Gleason–Yamabe
theorem, this is equivalent to `hilbert_smith_conjecture`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 22 57 58]
theorem hilbert_smith_padic_formulation {n : ℕ} (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) X]
    [AddAction (PadicInt p) X] [ContinuousVAdd (PadicInt p) X]
    [FaithfulVAdd (PadicInt p) X] :
    False := by
  sorry

/-- **Hilbert's fifth problem** (Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin, 1952): every Hausdorff,
second-countable topological group modeled on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space is continuously
isomorphic to a real-analytic Lie group.

The input `ChartedSpace` supplies only a topological atlas. The compatible analytic atlas and
analytic group operations belong to the output `LieGroupPresentation`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 22 57]
theorem hilbert_fifth_problem
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [T2Space G] [SecondCountableTopology G]
    [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G] :
    Nonempty (LieGroupPresentation G n) := by
  sorry

end Hilbert5
